milky_way.name: Milky Way
milky_way.title: Milky Way Galaxy
milky_way.description: The Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy, home to our Solar System. It contains billions of stars, gas, and dust, with a supermassive black hole at its center.

solar_system.name: Solar System
solar_system.title: Solar System
solar_system.description: The Solar System is the gravitationally bound system of the Sun and the objects that orbit it, including eight planets, dwarf planets, and countless smaller bodies.

alpha_centauri.name: Alpha Centauri
alpha_centauri.title: Alpha Centauri System
alpha_centauri.description: Alpha Centauri is the closest star system to our Solar System, located about 4.37 light-years away. It consists of three stars: Alpha Centauri A, Alpha Centauri B, and Proxima Centauri.

sagittarius_a.name: Sagittarius A*
sagittarius_a.title: Sagittarius A* Supermassive Black Hole
sagittarius_a.description: Sagittarius A* is a supermassive black hole located at the Galactic Center of the Milky Way galaxy. It is a highly compact and bright astronomical radio source.

sun.name: Sun
sun.description: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system, comprising 99.8% of the system's total mass. It is a nearly perfect sphere of hot plasma, heated to incandescence by nuclear fusion reactions in its core, which radiates energy primarily as light, ultraviolet, and infrared radiation, providing the primary source of energy for life on Earth.

mercury.name: Mercury
mercury.description: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system and the closest to the Sun. It experiences extreme temperature fluctuations, ranging from scorching days to freezing nights, and possesses a heavily cratered, ancient surface with no atmosphere and no moons.

venus.name: Venus
venus.description: Venus is the second planet from the Sun and Earth's closest planetary neighbor. It is enveloped in a thick, toxic atmosphere of carbon dioxide and sulfuric acid clouds that trap heat in a runaway greenhouse effect, making its surface hot enough to melt lead and making it the hottest planet in the solar system.

earth.name: Earth
earth.description: Earth is the third planet from the Sun and the only known astronomical object to harbor life. It is characterized by its liquid water oceans, which cover about 71% of its surface, an atmosphere rich in nitrogen and oxygen, and a strong magnetic field that shields it from harmful solar radiation.

moon.name: Moon
moon.description: The Moon is Earth's only natural satellite and the fifth-largest moon in the solar system. It is tidally locked to Earth, meaning it always shows the same face, and its gravitational pull is the primary driver of Earth's ocean tides and stabilizes the planet's axial tilt.

iss.name: International Space Station
iss.description: The International Space Station (ISS) is a modular space station in low Earth orbit. It is a multinational collaborative project involving five participating space agencies: NASA, Roscosmos, JAXA, ESA, and CSA. It serves as a microgravity and space environment research laboratory in which scientific tests are conducted.

mars.name: Mars
mars.description: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun and the second-smallest planet in the solar system. Often called the Red Planet due to the iron oxide prevalent on its surface, it is a cold desert world with a thin carbon dioxide atmosphere, seasonal polar ice caps, and extinct volcanoes like Olympus Mons.

phobos.name: Phobos
phobos.description: Phobos is the larger and closer of Mars' two small, irregularly shaped moons. It orbits so close to Mars that it completes three orbits in a single Martian day, and tidal forces are gradually drawing it closer to the planet, destined to crash into Mars or shatter into a ring.

deimos.name: Deimos
deimos.description: Deimos is the smaller and outer of Mars' two moons. It has a heavily cratered but smooth appearance due to a thick layer of pulverised rock dust (regolith) filling its craters, and its orbit is nearly circular and stable, unlike Phobos.

jupiter.name: Jupiter
jupiter.description: Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in our solar system, with a mass more than double that of all other planets combined. As a gas giant, it consists primarily of hydrogen and helium, has no well-defined solid surface, and is famous for its colorful bands of clouds and the Great Red Spot storm.

io.name: Io
io.description: Io is the innermost of Jupiter's four Galilean moons and the most volcanically active body in the solar system. Its intense activity is driven by tidal heating from gravitational friction with Jupiter and neighboring moons, resulting in hundreds of active volcanoes venting sulfur and sulfur dioxide.

europa.name: Europa
europa.description: Europa is the smallest of Jupiter's Galilean moons. Its surface is a highly reflective sheet of water ice crisscrossed by cracks (lineae), beneath which scientists believe a global, liquid water ocean exists containing twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans combined, making it a prime target for astrobiology.

ganymede.name: Ganymede
ganymede.description: Ganymede is the largest moon in our solar system, even exceeding the planet Mercury in size. It is the only natural satellite known to possess its own magnetic field, generated by convection in its liquid iron core, and features a mixture of dark, cratered terrain and lighter, grooved regions.

callisto.name: Callisto
callisto.description: Callisto is the second-largest moon of Jupiter and the third-largest in the solar system. It is the most heavily cratered object in the solar system, with an ancient surface showing no signs of geological activity, though it may harbor a salty ocean deep beneath its icy crust.

amalthea.name: Amalthea
amalthea.description: Amalthea is an irregularly shaped, reddish inner moon of Jupiter. It is extremely dark and porous, and radiates more heat than it receives from the Sun, possibly due to tidal friction or electric currents induced by Jupiter's powerful magnetic field.

himalia.name: Himalia
himalia.description: Himalia is the largest of Jupiter's irregular satellites, orbiting at a much greater distance than the Galilean moons. Discovered in 1904, it has a grey surface similar to C-type asteroids, indicating it is likely a captured asteroid from the outer solar system.

thebe.name: Thebe
thebe.description: Thebe is the fourth of Jupiter's inner moons by distance. It is irregularly shaped, orbits just outside Jupiter's main ring, and is heavily cratered with several large impact basins on its surface, releasing dust that feeds Jupiter's gossamer rings.

elara.name: Elara
elara.description: Elara is a prograde irregular moon of Jupiter. It orbits the planet at an average distance of nearly 11.7 million kilometers and has a diameter of about 86 kilometers, sharing a similar composition and origin to Himalia.

saturn.name: Saturn
saturn.description: Saturn is the sixth planet from the Sun and the second-largest in the solar system. It is a gas giant with a density lower than water, renowned for its spectacular, extensive ring system composed of billions of ice particles, rocky debris, and dust.

titan.name: Titan
titan.description: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and the second-largest moon in the solar system. It is unique for its dense nitrogen-rich atmosphere and a surface featuring stable lakes, rivers, and seas of liquid methane and ethane, making it the only body besides Earth with stable liquids on its surface.

rhea.name: Rhea
rhea.description: Rhea is the second-largest moon of Saturn, composed primarily of water ice with a small amount of rock. It has a heavily cratered surface and a very thin, tenuous atmosphere containing oxygen and carbon dioxide, detected by the Cassini spacecraft.

enceladus.name: Enceladus
enceladus.description: Enceladus is an active, icy moon of Saturn that reflects nearly 100% of the sunlight it receives. It features a global subsurface ocean beneath its crust, which erupts through fissures in the south polar region as geysers of water vapor, ice particles, and organic compounds.

mimas.name: Mimas
mimas.description: Mimas is a small, cratered moon of Saturn composed mostly of water ice. It is dominated by the colossal Herschel impact crater, which spans nearly a third of the moon's diameter, giving it an appearance strikingly similar to the Death Star from Star Wars.

tethys.name: Tethys
tethys.description: Tethys is a mid-sized Saturnian moon composed almost entirely of water ice. Its surface is scarred by the massive Odysseus impact basin and Ithaca Chasma, a giant canyon system that stretches across three-quarters of the moon's circumference.

dione.name: Dione
dione.description: Dione is a Saturnian moon with a heavily cratered leading hemisphere and a trailing hemisphere covered by bright, wispy ice cliffs. It is tidally locked and shares its orbit with two co-orbital moons, Helene and Polydeuces.

iapetus.name: Iapetus
iapetus.description: Iapetus is the third-largest moon of Saturn, famous for its dramatic two-tone coloration, with one hemisphere dark as coal and the other bright as snow. It also features a unique equatorial ridge that runs along its equator, reaching heights of 20 kilometers.

uranus.name: Uranus
uranus.description: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun, an ice giant with a pale cyan hue caused by methane in its atmosphere. It is unique for its extreme axial tilt of 97.8 degrees, causing it to rotate virtually on its side, resulting in extreme seasonal variations.

titania.name: Titania
titania.description: Titania is the largest moon of Uranus and the eighth-largest moon in the solar system. It is composed of roughly equal amounts of ice and rock, and its surface is marked by a network of massive faults, canyons, and scarps indicating past geological activity.

oberon.name: Oberon
oberon.description: Oberon is the outermost major moon of Uranus and the second-largest. It has an ancient, heavily cratered surface that shows little sign of internal activity, except for dark material of unknown origin covering the floors of many craters.

ariel.name: Ariel
ariel.description: Ariel is the brightest and youngest of Uranus's major moons. Its surface features complex networks of intersecting valleys, canyons, and smooth plains, suggesting a history of cryovolcanic resurfacing and tectonic activity.

umbriel.name: Umbriel
umbriel.description: Umbriel is the darkest of Uranus's major moons, reflecting only about half as much light as Ariel. It is heavily cratered and has an ancient surface, with its most prominent feature being a bright ring of material (Wunda) inside a crater.

miranda.name: Miranda
miranda.description: Miranda is the smallest and innermost of Uranus's major moons. It features an incredibly complex and bizarre geology with giant canyons, cliffs up to 20 kilometers deep, and mismatched terrains that suggest a chaotic history of impact disruption and tidal heating.

neptune.name: Neptune
neptune.description: Neptune is the eighth and most distant planet from the Sun. It is a cold, dark ice giant known for its deep blue color, dynamic atmosphere with supersonic winds up to 2,100 km/h, and a faint system of rings and ring arcs.

triton.name: Triton
triton.description: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune and the only large moon in the solar system that orbits in the opposite direction of its planet's rotation (retrograde orbit). It is volcanically active, with nitrogen geysers erupting from its freezing nitrogen-ice surface.

proteus.name: Proteus
proteus.description: Proteus is the second-largest moon of Neptune, orbiting very close to the planet. It is a highly irregular, dark body with a heavily cratered surface, and is so massive that it is close to the limit where its own gravity would pull it into a sphere.

nereid.name: Nereid
nereid.description: Nereid is one of Neptune's outer moons, discovered by Gerard Kuiper in 1949. It is famous for having one of the most eccentric orbits of any moon in the solar system, ranging from 1.3 million to 9.6 million kilometers from Neptune.

pluto.name: Pluto
pluto.description: Pluto is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper Belt, a region of icy bodies beyond Neptune. Once classified as the ninth planet, it has a complex surface of nitrogen ice plains, water ice mountains, and a thin atmosphere of nitrogen, methane, and carbon monoxide.

charon.name: Charon
charon.description: Charon is the largest of Pluto's five moons, half the size of Pluto itself. Because of their similar masses, Pluto and Charon orbit a common barycenter outside Pluto's surface, making them a binary dwarf planet system, and they are mutually tidally locked.

nix.name: Nix
nix.description: Nix is a small, elongated moon of Pluto discovered in 2005. It orbits Pluto in a chaotic, tumbling rotation due to the rapidly changing gravitational forces exerted by the binary Pluto-Charon system.

hydra.name: Hydra
hydra.description: Hydra is the outermost and second-largest of Pluto's small moons, discovered in 2005. It is covered in highly reflective water ice, and like Nix, it lacks a stable rotation axis, tumbling unpredictably as it orbits the double-planet system.

kerberos.name: Kerberos
kerberos.description: Kerberos is a tiny, double-lobed moon of Pluto orbiting between Nix and Hydra. Discovered in 2011 by the Hubble Space Telescope, its shape suggests it was formed by the low-velocity merger of two smaller, icy bodies.

styx.name: Styx
styx.description: Styx is the smallest moon of Pluto, discovered in 2012 by the Hubble Space Telescope during preparations for the New Horizons flyby. It has a highly irregular shape and orbits in the plane of the other Pluto moons.

ceres.name: Ceres
ceres.description: Ceres is the largest object in the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter and the only dwarf planet located in the inner solar system. It is composed of ice and rock, with evidence of a subsurface ocean and cryovolcanism, such as bright sodium carbonate deposits in Occator Crater.

asteriod.name: Asteroid Belt
asteriod.title: Asteroid Belt
asteriod.description: The Asteroid Belt is a torus-shaped region in the Solar System, located roughly between the orbits of the planets Jupiter and Mars.

kuiper.name: Kuiper Belt
kuiper.title: Kuiper Belt
kuiper.description: The Kuiper Belt is a circumstellar disc in the outer Solar System, extending from the orbit of Neptune.

oort.name: Oort Cloud
oort.title: Oort Cloud
oort.description: The Oort Cloud is a theoretical spherical cloud of predominantly icy planetesimals proposed to surround the Sun at extreme distances in the outer reaches of the Solar System.

haumea.name: Haumea
haumea.description: Haumea is a dwarf planet located beyond Neptune's orbit in the Kuiper Belt. Notable for its extremely fast rotation, completing a turn in under four hours, its rapid spin has stretched it into an elongated ellipsoid shape. It also features a thin ring system and a high-albedo icy surface.

makemake.name: Makemake
makemake.description: Makemake is the second-brightest Kuiper Belt object after Pluto. Named after the creator deity of the Rapa Nui people of Easter Island, Makemake lacks a substantial atmosphere and is covered by a layer of extremely cold methane and ethane ice, giving it a reddish hue.

eris.name: Eris
eris.description: Eris is one of the most massive known dwarf planets in the solar system, located in the scattered disc beyond the Kuiper Belt. Its discovery in 2005 sparked the astronomical debate that ultimately led the IAU to redefine the definition of a planet and reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet.

gonggong.name: Gonggong
gonggong.description: Gonggong is a large dwarf planet candidate in the scattered disc beyond Neptune. Known for its reddish surface caused by organic compounds (tholins) and water ice, it has a single known moon named Xiangliu.

xiangliu.name: Xiangliu
xiangliu.description: Xiangliu is the only known moon of the dwarf planet Gonggong. Named after a venomous nine-headed serpent monster in Chinese mythology, it orbits Gonggong at a distance of about 24,000 kilometers.

quaoar.name: Quaoar
quaoar.description: Quaoar is a Kuiper Belt object notable for possessing a rare, dense ring system located far outside its Roche limit. It is accompanied by its small moon, Weywot, and features a surface coated in water ice and methane.

weywot.name: Weywot
weywot.description: Weywot is the only known satellite of Quaoar. Named after the Tongva god of the sky, Weywot is thought to be a fragment created from a giant collision that Quaoar experienced in the past.

sedna.name: Sedna
sedna.description: Sedna is one of the most distant known objects in the Solar System, possessing an extremely elongated orbit that takes over 11,000 years to complete. Its orbit takes it from 76 AU at its closest point to nearly 1,000 AU at its farthest.

orcus.name: Orcus
orcus.description: Orcus is a large Kuiper Belt object often called the 'anti-Pluto' because its orbit has the same period and inclination as Pluto's, but is oriented in opposite phase so that when Orcus is closest to the Sun, Pluto is farthest.

salacia.name: Salacia
salacia.description: Salacia is a large Kuiper Belt object and borderline dwarf planet candidate. It has an exceptionally dark surface with an albedo of around 4%, indicating a lack of bright volatile ices like methane.

alpha_centauri_a.name: Alpha Centauri A
alpha_centauri_a.description: Alpha Centauri A is the principal component of the triple star system Alpha Centauri. It is a solar-type yellow main-sequence star, slightly larger and more luminous than the Sun.

alpha_centauri_b.name: Alpha Centauri B
alpha_centauri_b.description: Alpha Centauri B is the secondary star of the Alpha Centauri binary system. It is an orange main-sequence star, slightly smaller and cooler than the Sun.

proxima_centauri.name: Proxima Centauri
proxima_centauri.description: Proxima Centauri is a small, low-mass red dwarf star located in the constellation of Centaurus. It is the closest known star to the Sun.

proxima_centauri_b.name: Proxima Centauri b
proxima_centauri_b.description: Proxima Centauri b is an exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of the red dwarf star Proxima Centauri. It is the closest known exoplanet to the Solar System.

proxima_centauri_c.name: Proxima Centauri c
proxima_centauri_c.description: Proxima Centauri c is a candidate super-Earth or mini-Neptune orbiting Proxima Centauri at a distance of roughly 1.5 AU.

proxima_centauri_d.name: Proxima Centauri d
proxima_centauri_d.description: Proxima Centauri d is a sub-Earth exoplanet orbiting very close to Proxima Centauri, completing an orbit every 5.1 days.

alpha_centauri_a_b.name: Alpha Centauri Ab
alpha_centauri_a_b.description: Alpha Centauri Ab is a candidate exoplanet orbiting in the habitable zone of Alpha Centauri A.

halley.name: Halley
halley.description: Halley's Comet is a short-period comet visible from Earth every 75–76 years. It is the only known short-period comet that is regularly visible to the naked eye from Earth.

trappist-1.name: TRAPPIST-1
trappist-1.title: TRAPPIST-1 System
trappist-1.description: TRAPPIST-1 is an ultra-cool red dwarf star with seven Earth-sized terrestrial planets orbiting it. It has the largest number of Earth-sized planets found in a single planetary system.

trappist-1b.name: TRAPPIST-1b
trappist-1b.description: TRAPPIST-1b is the innermost and most massive planet of the TRAPPIST-1 system. It orbits very close to its star, making it a scorching hot world.

trappist-1c.name: TRAPPIST-1c
trappist-1c.description: TRAPPIST-1c is a rocky, Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting the ultra-cool dwarf star TRAPPIST-1. It is the most massive planet in the system.

trappist-1d.name: TRAPPIST-1d
trappist-1d.description: TRAPPIST-1d is one of the least massive planets in the TRAPPIST-1 system and orbits near the inner edge of the habitable zone.

trappist-1e.name: TRAPPIST-1e
trappist-1e.description: TRAPPIST-1e is a rocky, Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting within the habitable zone of TRAPPIST-1, making it one of the most promising candidates for potential habitability.

trappist-1f.name: TRAPPIST-1f
trappist-1f.description: TRAPPIST-1f is an Earth-sized exoplanet orbiting in the habitable zone. It is thought to potentially possess a significant amount of water.

trappist-1g.name: TRAPPIST-1g
trappist-1g.description: TRAPPIST-1g is the largest planet in the habitable zone of TRAPPIST-1. It completes an orbit roughly every 12 days.

trappist-1h.name: TRAPPIST-1h
trappist-1h.description: TRAPPIST-1h is the outermost known planet of the TRAPPIST-1 system. It is also the smallest and coldest, orbiting far from the star's warmth.

lich.name: Lich
lich.title: Lich (PSR B1257+12) System
lich.description: PSR B1257+12, designated Lich, is a millisecond pulsar located 2,300 light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It is famous for hosting the first confirmed extrasolar planetary system.

draugr.name: Draugr
draugr.description: Draugr (PSR B1257+12 b) is the innermost exoplanet of the Lich system. With a mass roughly 0.02 times Earth, it is one of the least massive exoplanets ever discovered.

poltergeist.name: Poltergeist
poltergeist.description: Poltergeist (PSR B1257+12 c) is a super-Earth exoplanet orbiting Lich at 0.36 AU with an orbital period of about 66.3 days.

phobetor.name: Phobetor
phobetor.description: Phobetor (PSR B1257+12 d) is a super-Earth exoplanet orbiting Lich at 0.47 AU with an orbital period of about 98.2 days.

s2.name: S2 (S0-2)
s2.description: S2 is a B-type main sequence star orbiting the supermassive black hole Sagittarius A* in a 16.05-year period. Its orbit provided key evidence for Schwarzschild precession and gravitational redshift predicted by Einstein's General Relativity.

s4716.name: S4716
s4716.description: S4716 is a star orbiting Sagittarius A* with a period of just 9.9 years, reaching peak velocities of 8,000 km/s (~2.7% the speed of light).

s62.name: S62
s62.description: S62 is a high-velocity star orbiting Sagittarius A* with an orbital period of approximately 9.9 years.

s55.name: S55 (S0-102)
s55.description: S55 is a star orbiting Sagittarius A* with an orbital period of approximately 12.8 years.

s14.name: S14 (S0-16)
s14.description: S14 is a star featuring a close pericenter approach to Sagittarius A* down to 45 AU.

s4711.name: S4711
s4711.description: S4711 is a high-velocity star orbiting Sagittarius A* with a short 7.6-year period.

voyager_1.name: Voyager 1
voyager_1.description: Voyager 1 is a space probe launched by NASA on September 5, 1977. It became the first human-made object to enter interstellar space in 2012 and remains the most distant human-made object from Earth.

voyager_2.name: Voyager 2
voyager_2.description: Voyager 2 is a NASA space probe launched on August 20, 1977. It is the only spacecraft to have visited all four gas giant planets of the Solar System (Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune) before crossing into interstellar space in 2018.

new_horizons.name: New Horizons
new_horizons.description: New Horizons is a NASA space probe launched on January 19, 2006. It performed a historic flyby of Pluto and its moons in July 2015, capturing the first high-resolution images of the dwarf planet, and later explored the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth in 2019.

mount_everest.name: Mount Everest
mount_everest.description: Earth's highest mountain above sea level (8,848 m), located in the Himalayas on the border between Nepal and Tibet.

mount_aconcagua.name: Mount Aconcagua
mount_aconcagua.description: The highest mountain in South America (6,961 m), located in the Andes mountain range in Argentina.

mount_denali.name: Mount Denali
mount_denali.description: The highest mountain peak in North America (6,190 m), located in the Alaska Range, USA.

mount_kilimanjaro.name: Mount Kilimanjaro
mount_kilimanjaro.description: The highest free-standing mountain in the world and the tallest peak in Africa (5,895 m), located in Tanzania.

mount_elbrus.name: Mount Elbrus
mount_elbrus.description: A dormant volcano and the highest peak in Europe (5,642 m), located in the Caucasus Mountains, Russia.

mount_vinson.name: Vinson Massif
mount_vinson.description: The highest peak in Antarctica (4,892 m), located in the Ellsworth Mountains.

mount_cartenz.name: Carstensz Pyramid
mount_cartenz.description: The highest peak in Oceania/Australasia (4,884 m), located in the Jayawijaya Mountains, Papua, Indonesia.

mount_k2.name: Mount K2
mount_k2.description: The second-highest mountain on Earth (8,611 m), located in the Karakoram range on the border between Pakistan and China.

mont_blanc.name: Mont Blanc
mont_blanc.description: The highest peak in the Alps and Western Europe (4,807 m), rising on the border between France and Italy.

mauna_loa.name: Mauna Loa
mauna_loa.description: The largest active shield volcano on Earth by volume and surface area, located on the island of Hawaii.

patagonian_desert.name: Patagonian Desert
patagonian_desert.description: The largest desert in South America, spanning across the Patagonian region of Argentina and Chile.

atacama_desert.name: Atacama Desert
atacama_desert.description: The driest non-polar desert on Earth, located in Chile, famous for its Mars-like landscape and major astronomical observatories.

gobi_desert.name: Gobi Desert
gobi_desert.description: A vast cold desert in Central Asia spanning parts of China and Mongolia, famous for its Silk Road history and dinosaur fossil sites.

arabian_desert.name: Arabian Desert
arabian_desert.description: A vast desert landscape in the Arabian Peninsula containing the world's largest continuous sand desert, Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter).

great_basin_desert.name: Great Basin Desert
great_basin_desert.description: The largest desert in North America, forming part of the Great Basin region in the United States.

kalahari_desert.name: Kalahari Desert
kalahari_desert.description: A large semi-arid sandy savanna in Southern Africa extending across Botswana, Namibia, and South Africa.

great_victoria_desert.name: Great Victoria Desert
great_victoria_desert.description: The largest desert in Australia, characterized by red sand dunes and salt lakes.

caspian_sea.name: Caspian Sea
caspian_sea.description: The world's largest inland body of water by surface area, located between Europe and Asia.

atlantic_ocean.name: Atlantic Ocean
atlantic_ocean.description: The second-largest ocean in the world, separating the Americas from Europe and Africa.

pacific_ocean.name: Pacific Ocean
pacific_ocean.description: The largest and deepest ocean on Earth, extending from the Arctic Ocean in the north to the Southern Ocean in the south.

indian_ocean.name: Indian Ocean
indian_ocean.description: The third-largest ocean in the world, bounded by Asia, Africa, Australia, and the Southern Ocean.

mediterranean_sea.name: Mediterranean Sea
mediterranean_sea.description: A sea connected to the Atlantic Ocean, surrounded by the Mediterranean Basin and almost completely enclosed by land.

baltic_sea.name: Baltic Sea
baltic_sea.description: An arm of the Atlantic Ocean in Northern Europe, enclosed by Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Russia, and Sweden.

black_sea.name: Black Sea
black_sea.description: An inland sea located between Southeastern Europe and Western Asia, connected to the Atlantic Ocean via the Mediterranean.

red_sea.name: Red Sea
red_sea.description: A seawater inlet of the Indian Ocean lying between Africa and Asia, known for its high salinity and rich marine life.

persian_gulf.name: Persian Gulf
persian_gulf.description: A mediterranean sea in Western Asia, connected to the Gulf of Oman by the Strait of Hormuz.

gulf_of_mexico.name: Gulf of Mexico
gulf_of_mexico.description: An ocean basin and marginal sea of the Atlantic Ocean, largely surrounded by the North American continent.

greenland.name: Greenland
greenland.description: The world's largest island, located between the Arctic and Atlantic Oceans, covered mostly by a massive ice sheet.

antarctic_desert.name: Antarctic Desert
antarctic_desert.description: The largest and coldest desert in the world, covering the continent of Antarctica with extremely low precipitation and humidity.

victoria_falls.name: Victoria Falls
victoria_falls.description: A spectacular waterfall on the Zambezi River on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe, one of the world's largest sheets of falling water.

niagara_falls.name: Niagara Falls
niagara_falls.description: A famous group of three massive waterfalls spanning the border between the United States and Canada.

point_nemo.name: Point Nemo
point_nemo.description: The oceanic pole of inaccessibility, the most remote place on Earth's oceans, located in the South Pacific Ocean.

amazon_rainforest.name: Amazon Rainforest
amazon_rainforest.description: The world's largest tropical rainforest, spanning across much of the Amazon basin in South America and producing a vast percentage of Earth's oxygen.

congo_rainforest.name: Congo Rainforest
congo_rainforest.description: The second-largest tropical rainforest in the world, spanning the Congo Basin in Central Africa and home to rich biodiversity.

chicxulub_crater.name: Chicxulub Crater
chicxulub_crater.description: An ancient asteroid impact crater buried beneath the Yucatán Peninsula in Mexico. The colossal impact triggered the mass extinction of dinosaurs 66 million years ago.

sahara_desert.name: Sahara Desert
sahara_desert.description: The world's largest hot desert covering most of Northern Africa, renowned for its massive sand dunes and hyper-arid climate.

nile_river.name: Nile River
nile_river.description: The longest river in Africa and one of the longest in the world, flowing northward into the Mediterranean Sea and sustaining ancient Egyptian civilization.

grand_canyon.name: Grand Canyon
grand_canyon.description: A immense steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River in Arizona, USA, revealing billions of years of geological rock layers.

mariana_trench.name: Mariana Trench
mariana_trench.description: The deepest known oceanic trench on Earth, reaching nearly 11,000 meters deep at Challenger Deep in the Western Pacific Ocean.

pyramids_giza.name: Pyramids of Giza
pyramids_giza.description: An ancient pyramid complex in Egypt built as royal tombs for pharaohs, including the iconic Great Pyramid of Giza.

great_barrier_reef.name: Great Barrier Reef
great_barrier_reef.description: The world's largest coral reef system, located in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland, Australia.

himalaya_mountains.name: Himalaya Mountains
himalaya_mountains.description: A major mountain range in Asia separating the plains of the Indian subcontinent from the Tibetan Plateau, containing Earth's highest peaks.

alps_mountains.name: Alps Mountains
alps_mountains.description: The highest and most extensive mountain range system that lies entirely in Europe, stretching across eight Alpine countries.

andes_mountains.name: Andes Mountains
andes_mountains.description: The longest continental mountain range in the world, forming a continuous highland along the western edge of South America.

rocky_mountains.name: Rocky Mountains
rocky_mountains.description: A major mountain range in western North America stretching more than 4,800 kilometers from Canada to the United States.

caucasus_mountains.name: Caucasus Mountains
caucasus_mountains.description: A mountain system at the intersection of Europe and Asia, stretching between the Black Sea and the Caspian Sea.

atlas_mountains.name: Atlas Mountains
atlas_mountains.description: A mountain range in North Africa extending through Morocco, Algeria, and Tunisia, separating the Mediterranean and Atlantic coastlines from the Sahara Desert.

ural_mountains.name: Ural Mountains
ural_mountains.description: A mountain range running from north to south through western Russia, traditionally considered the boundary between Europe and Asia.

lake_victoria.name: Lake Victoria
lake_victoria.description: The largest lake in Africa by surface area and the world's second-largest freshwater lake, located in East Africa.

zagros_mountains.name: Zagros Mountains
zagros_mountains.description: A major mountain range in Iran, Iraq, and southeastern Turkey, stretching over 1,600 kilometers along the Iranian Plateau.

mount_olympus.name: Olympus Mons
mount_olympus.description: A gigantic shield volcano on Mars, the highest volcano and planetary mountain known in the entire Solar System (~21.9 km tall).

valles_marineris.name: Valles Marineris
valles_marineris.description: A vast canyon system on Mars stretching over 4,000 km, dwarfing Earth's Grand Canyon.

gale_crater.name: Gale Crater
gale_crater.description: A large impact crater on Mars and the landing site for NASA's Curiosity rover, featuring Mount Sharp at its center.

jezero_crater.name: Jezero Crater
jezero_crater.description: An ancient lake and river delta on Mars, landing site for NASA's Perseverance rover searching for signs of ancient microbial life.

hellas_planitia.name: Hellas Planitia
hellas_planitia.description: A colossal impact basin roughly 2,300 km in diameter located in Mars' southern hemisphere, one of the largest impact craters in the Solar System.

ascraeus_mons.name: Ascraeus Mons
ascraeus_mons.description: The northernmost and tallest volcano of the Tharsis Montes trio (~18 km high) on Mars.

pavonis_mons.name: Pavonis Mons
pavonis_mons.description: The middle shield volcano of the Tharsis Montes trio (~14 km high), situated almost directly on Mars' equator.

arsia_mons.name: Arsia Mons
arsia_mons.description: The southernmost volcano of the Tharsis Montes trio (~12 km high), featuring a massive caldera and ancient volcanic pit craters.

medusa_fossae.name: Medusae Fossae Formation
medusa_fossae.description: A vast, soft geological formation along Mars' equator composed of wind-eroded volcanic ash deposits, potentially harboring deep subsurface water ice.

nili_fossae.name: Nili Fossae
nili_fossae.description: A complex geological fracture system on Mars rich in clay minerals and olivine, indicating an ancient water-rich environment.

ghost_dunes.name: Ghost Dunes
ghost_dunes.description: Ancient sand dune casts in Noctis Labyrinthus and Hellas preserved when lava or sediment flooded around them millions of years ago, leaving negative dune molds.

meridiani_planum.name: Meridiani Planum
meridiani_planum.description: A vast plain located at Mars' equator rich in grey hematite deposits, site of extensive exploration by NASA's Opportunity rover.

hale_crater.name: Hale Crater
hale_crater.description: A 125 km wide impact crater in Margaritifer Terra with dramatic terraced walls and recurring slope lineae (RSL) hinting at seasonal saltwater flows.

aram_chaos.name: Aram Chaos
aram_chaos.description: An ancient 280 km wide crater collapsed into a vast chaos terrain, holding rich deposits of hematite and water-bearing sulfates.

aurorae_chaos.name: Aurorae Chaos
aurorae_chaos.description: A massive broken chaos terrain east of Valles Marineris created by colossal ancient groundwater outbursts.

aureum_chaos.name: Aureum Chaos
aureum_chaos.description: A vast, heavily eroded chaotic canyon system with layered mesas and deep troughs formed by catastrophic ancient flooding.

planum_boreum.name: Planum Boreum
planum_boreum.description: The northern polar plain of Mars consisting of permanent water and carbon dioxide ice caps, featuring dramatic spiral troughs (Chasma Boreale).

alba_mons.name: Alba Mons
alba_mons.description: A unique volcano on Mars with the largest surface area footprint (~1,600 km diameter) but extremely gentle slopes formed by fluid lava flows.

elysium_mons.name: Elysium Mons
elysium_mons.description: The major volcano in the Elysium volcanic province (~13.9 km high), towering high above the surrounding Elysium Planitia plains.

planum_australe.name: Planum Australe
planum_australe.description: The southern polar plain of Mars covered by thick permanent water ice and seasonal carbon dioxide ice, famous for spring CO2 geysers creating dark spider-like patterns.

utopia_planitia.name: Utopia Planitia
utopia_planitia.description: A vast plain within a giant impact basin in the northern hemisphere of Mars, famous as the landing site for Viking 2 (1976) and China's Zhurong rover (2021).

giant_red_spot.name: Great Red Spot
giant_red_spot.description: A persistent giant anticyclonic storm in Jupiter's atmosphere that is larger than Earth and has raged for centuries.

great_dark_spot.name: Great Dark Spot
great_dark_spot.description: A giant anticyclonic storm in Neptune's atmosphere first observed by NASA's Voyager 2 spacecraft in 1989.

tranquility_base.name: Statio Tranquillitatis
tranquility_base.description: The historic landing site of Apollo 11 in 1969 on the Moon, where humans (Neil Armstrong & Buzz Aldrin) first stepped on another world.

tycho_crater.name: Tycho Crater
tycho_crater.description: A prominent young impact crater in the southern lunar highlands with an extensive bright ray system visible from Earth.

copernicus_crater.name: Copernicus Crater
copernicus_crater.description: A striking impact crater in Oceanus Procellarum featuring a prominent central peak and extensive bright ray system.

mare_imbrium.name: Mare Imbrium
mare_imbrium.description: A massive, dark lava plain created by ancient impact flooding, forming one of the most prominent features on the Moon's near side.

plato_crater.name: Plato Crater
plato_crater.description: A prominent 100 km wide impact crater on the northern shore of Mare Imbrium with a smooth, dark lava-filled floor.

montes_apenninus.name: Montes Apenninus
montes_apenninus.description: A dramatic mountain range on the Moon with peaks reaching up to 5 km high, forming the southeastern border of the Mare Imbrium basin.

mare_serenitatis.name: Mare Serenitatis
mare_serenitatis.description: A 674 km wide circular lunar mare located within the Serenitatis basin to the northeast of Mare Imbrium.

mare_tranquillitatis.name: Mare Tranquillitatis
mare_tranquillitatis.description: A famous basaltic plain and landing site of Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base), exhibiting a bluish tint due to high titanium concentrations.

mare_crisium.name: Mare Crisium
mare_crisium.description: An isolated 556 km wide circular lunar mare located in the Crisium basin, easily recognized near the Moon's northeastern limb.

mare_fecunditatis.name: Mare Fecunditatis
mare_fecunditatis.description: A large 840 km wide lunar mare basin in the southeastern near side of the Moon formed during the ancient Nectarian epoch.

mare_nectaris.name: Mare Nectaris
mare_nectaris.description: A small lunar mare located south of Mare Tranquillitatis, framed by the Pyrenaeus mountains and the ancient Fracastorius crater.

mare_vaporum.name: Mare Vaporum
mare_vaporum.description: A 245 km wide lunar mare located southwest of Mare Serenitatis near the center of the Moon's near side.

mare_nubium.name: Mare Nubium
mare_nubium.description: An ancient 715 km wide circular lunar mare located in the Nubium basin in the southwestern near side.

langrenus_crater.name: Langrenus Crater
langrenus_crater.description: A prominent 132 km wide impact crater on the eastern shore of Mare Fecunditatis featuring terraced walls and bright central peaks.

stevinus_crater.name: Stevinus Crater
stevinus_crater.description: A 75 km wide impact crater in the southeastern lunar highlands featuring steep inner slopes and bright rayed satellite craters.

mare_humorum.name: Mare Humorum
mare_humorum.description: A circular 389 km wide lunar mare basin surrounded by the prominent Gassendi crater and concentric rille systems.

mare_frigoris.name: Mare Frigoris
mare_frigoris.description: An elongated northern lunar mare stretching across the far north of Mare Imbrium and Mare Serenitatis.

oceanus_procellarum.name: Oceanus Procellarum
oceanus_procellarum.description: A vast lunar ocean spanning over 2,500 km across the western edge of the near side, the largest basaltic maria plain on the Moon.

aristarchus_crater.name: Aristarchus Crater
aristarchus_crater.description: The brightest impact crater on the lunar surface (40 km wide), situated on the elevated Aristarchus Plateau in Oceanus Procellarum.

kepler_crater.name: Kepler Crater
kepler_crater.description: A prominent young 31 km wide impact crater in Oceanus Procellarum surrounded by a prominent ray system.

mare_cognitum.name: Mare Cognitum
mare_cognitum.description: A 376 km wide lunar mare located in a basin within Oceanus Procellarum, site of historical impacts by Ranger 7 (1964) and landing of Apollo 12 (1969).

mare_insularum.name: Mare Insularum
mare_insularum.description: A 513 km wide lunar mare located south of Mare Imbrium and east of Oceanus Procellarum, hosting the famous Copernicus and Kepler craters.

zeeman_crater.name: Zeeman Crater
zeeman_crater.description: A massive 190 km wide impact crater near the Moon's south pole on the far side, featuring an extraordinarily high wall elevation.

tsiolkovskiy_crater.name: Tsiolkovskiy Crater
tsiolkovskiy_crater.description: A spectacular 185 km wide crater on the far side of the Moon featuring a dark basaltic floor and a high central peak.

mouton_mons.name: Mons Mouton
mouton_mons.description: A tall, flat-topped lunar mountain near the Moon's south pole, named after NASA mathematician Melba Mouton and prime candidate for lunar ice exploration.

south_pole_aitken.name: South Pole-Aitken Basin
south_pole_aitken.description: The oldest and largest impact basin on the Moon (2,500 km diameter), located on the lunar far side.

mare_orientale.name: Mare Orientale
mare_orientale.description: A giant multi-ringed impact basin located on the western border of the Moon's near and far sides.

mare_smythii.name: Mare Smythii
mare_smythii.description: A circular lunar mare located along the equator on the eastern limb of the Moon.

mare_marginis.name: Mare Marginis
mare_marginis.description: A lunar mare along the eastern limb of the Moon, located just north of Mare Smythii.

maat_mons.name: Maat Mons
maat_mons.description: The highest volcano on planet Venus (8 km high), exhibiting signs of relatively recent volcanic activity.

ishtar_terra.name: Ishtar Terra
ishtar_terra.description: One of two main continental highlands on Venus, located near the north pole and home to the Maxwell Montes range.

aphrodite_terra.name: Aphrodite Terra
aphrodite_terra.description: The largest continental highland region on planet Venus, stretching along the equator and roughly equal in size to the continent of Africa on Earth.

beta_regio.name: Beta Regio
beta_regio.description: A major volcanic highland region on Venus marked by two massive shield volcanoes (Theia Mons and Rhea Mons) and the Devana Chasma rift valley.

maxwell_montes.name: Maxwell Montes
maxwell_montes.description: The highest mountain range on planet Venus (~11 km high), situated on the highland mass of Ishtar Terra.

caloris_basin.name: Caloris Basin
caloris_basin.description: A colossal 1,550 km wide impact basin on Mercury, surrounded by high mountain rings formed by a giant asteroid impact.

tombaugh_regio.name: Tombaugh Regio
tombaugh_regio.description: The famous heart-shaped icy plain feature on Pluto's surface, largely composed of nitrogen ice.

occator_crater.name: Occator Crater
occator_crater.description: A crater on the dwarf planet Ceres famous for mysterious bright sodium carbonate spots (Cerealia Facula).
